question.text: What will be New England's spark spread on December 1, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the spark spread, in $/MWh, for delivery on December 1, 2026 for New England, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration's [Daily Prices](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/prices.php) page, based on its displayed prices for the New England electricity price in $/MWh and the New England natural gas price, in $/MMBtu.
question.fine_print: Please note that irrespective of the spark spread value displayed at the resolution source, the assumed efficiency of natural gas combined-cycle generation will be 7,000 Btu/kWh. Thus, the spark spread formula is E - 7G, where E = electricity price and G = natural gas price.

# New England spark spread on December 1, 2026: research brief

**Summary:** The latest spark spread is $37.54/MWh, as of November 6. New England gas is unusually cheap right now, at about $1.35/MMBtu. Winter forward prices, though, still expect Algonquin to trade at a large premium. Whether that premium shows up by Monday, November 30, which is when gas and power for December 1 delivery trade, will mostly decide the result.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-06: EIA's Daily Prices page, "Select Spot Prices for Delivery Today," shows these New England values. The other tables on the page are dated 11/05/26. [EIA](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/prices.php)
  - Electricity: $46.99/MWh, up 3.3%.
  - Natural gas: $1.35/MMBtu, up 3.1%.
  - Spark spread as displayed: $37.54/MWh. Using E - 7G: 46.99 - 9.45 = 37.54.
- For comparison on the same day: New York City $34.98, Mid-Atlantic $65.98, Midwest $31.65. [EIA](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/prices.php)
- December 1, 2026 is a Tuesday. Its prices should trade on Monday, November 30, the first trading day after the Thanksgiving weekend. This timing is my inference from the "delivery today" label.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The value depends on trading about 3 weeks from now.
- New England gas is at unusual lows for early November. Normal winter conditions could change the spread sharply. When gas jumps, 7G can rise faster than power prices, which narrows the spread or even turns it negative.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- About 2026-11-06: NGI says Northeast winter forward prices are falling. Peak winter prices are near $16/MMBtu at Algonquin Citygate, versus $7 at Transco Zone 6 NY. NGI notes mild weather could last into December. [NGI](https://naturalgasintel.com/news/natural-gas-forward-prices-slide-as-northeast-winter-premiums-retreat/)
- 2026-11-06: Carbon Brief says a "super El Niño" is on track to peak in December 2026, with a Niño3.4 anomaly of about 4°C. [Carbon Brief](https://www.carbonbrief.org/simply-staggering-rapidly-developing-super-el-nino-on-track-to-peak-in-december)
- Early November 2026, per NGI:
  - Algonquin was near $1/MMBtu, compared with about $3 a year earlier.
  - Algonquin Gas Transmission put an operational flow order in place on November 1 because of storage limits and excess supply.
  - Lower demand is keeping Canadian imports out. [NGI](https://naturalgasintel.com/news/storage-limits-force-northeast-natural-gas-pipelines-to-turn-away-excess-supply/), [NGI](https://naturalgasintel.com/news/sharply-lower-demand-keeps-canadian-imports-at-bay-natgas-prices-low-for-northeast/)
- About late October 2026: Algonquin's winter 2026/27 strip was $11.666/MMBtu, an $8.27 premium over Henry Hub. [NGI](https://naturalgasintel.com/news/winter-natural-gas-forwards-tumble-as-warmth-supply-glut-batter-prices/)
- Late October 2026, undated trade note: NYMEX December gas settled around $4.57/MMBtu. I could not verify the date. [Tiger/Reuters](https://www.itiger.com/news/2586026384)
- 2026-09-09: EIA reported:
  - Algonquin averaged 43¢ below Henry Hub from April through July 2026, the second-largest discount for that period since 1999.
  - Canadian imports reached a record 0.4 Bcf/d.
  - Wind generation was up 59% and solar up 29%. [EIA](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=68124)

## 4. Base rates
- I could not find exact EIA spark spread values for past December 1 dates. The page does not keep an archive I could reach.
- Late November to early December 2025, from EIA's weekly gas update:
  - Algonquin was $8.08 on November 26 and $25.00 on December 3, its highest since January 2025.
  - Henry Hub was $5.05 on December 1. [EIA NGWU](https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/weekly/archivenew_ngwu/2025/12_04)
- Power in the same period, from S&P: ISO-NE Internal Hub on-peak day-ahead power averaged $63.77/MWh in November 2025 and $161.97 in the week ending December 5, with a high of $212.24 on December 5. At $25 gas, 7G is $175, so the spread around that time was probably small or negative. That is my calculation, not a reported figure. [S&P](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/electric-power/120525-low-temperatures-push-up-us-northeast-power-gas-prices)
- Pattern: as winter starts, early-November spreads often in the $30 to $40 range can swing by tens of dollars within days when cold arrives. This year started far below past years: gas near $1 to $1.35, versus about $3 in November 2025 and $8 in late November 2025.
- Seasonal comparison over the last 3 to 5 years: I could not get the November 7 to December 1 path from verifiable sources beyond the 2025 figures above.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on New England spark spreads or Algonquin prices.
- The Kalshi markets supplied with the question cover snow in Trenton, Detroit and Minneapolis, US retail electricity prices and ERCOT demand. None of them match this question.
- Forward market: the Algonquin winter strip at about $11.7/MMBtu as of late October implies much higher gas than today's. I could not find a December 2026 Algonquin forward quote, and NGI's snapshot pages showed placeholder values.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Weather outlooks:
  - NOAA's December to February outlook favors above-normal temperatures in the Northeast, driven by a very strong El Niño. [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/new-super-el-nino-maps-show-potential-rainfall-temperatures-across-us-12353463), [AP/KPTV](https://www.kptv.com/2026/10/17/us-winter-is-likely-be-wetter-warmer-forecasters-say-if-you-want-more-snow-look-south/)
  - Fox Weather expects winter-like temperatures by late November or early December, but warns El Niño may delay them. [Fox Weather](https://www.foxweather.com/weather-news/millions-pleasant-november-above-average-temperatures-us)
  - NYNJPA Weather expects a mild December. [NYNJPA](https://nynjpaweather.com/public/2026/10/30/winter-forecast-2026-27/)
  - The Farmers' Almanac 60-day forecast for November 25-30 says "mild, then colder." [Almanac](https://www.almanac.com/weather/longrange/region/us/1)
  - I did not find a December-only outlook from NOAA's Climate Prediction Center. It normally comes out in mid-November, followed by the 8-14 day outlooks that cover November 30.
- Other things to watch:
  - Whether the Algonquin flow order is lifted.
  - Weekly EIA storage reports.
  - The NYMEX December contract expiring in late November.
  - Thanksgiving-weekend trading for Monday, November 30.

# New England spark spread on Dec 1, 2026: research brief

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-06: The EIA Daily Prices page lists New England electricity (Mass Hub, ISO-NE) at **$46.99/MWh**, up 3.3%, and Algonquin Citygate gas at **$1.35/MMBtu**, up 3.1%. EIA's spark spread is **$37.54/MWh**, which matches E - 7G (46.99 - 9.45). Other tables on the page are labeled "11/05/26 Close." [EIA](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/prices.php)
- The table shows prices "for delivery today." Dec 1, 2026 is a Tuesday, so the resolving prices will most likely be the ones traded Monday, Nov 30. This is my reading of the page, and EIA does not state it. Electricity on this page has historically been the ICE day-ahead on-peak price.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. It depends on Algonquin and Mass Hub prices about 3 weeks from now, and Algonquin swings a lot in early winter.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-06: NGI says New England cash gas is trading at about half of Henry Hub (around $2.60), with NYMEX futures back above $3. Mild weather and storage limits are the reasons given. [NGI](https://naturalgasintel.com/news/physical-natural-gas-prices-power-up-for-weekend/)
- Early Nov 2026: NGI puts Algonquin's November-to-date average at about $1.33, against roughly $3 a year earlier. Algonquin pipeline has had an operational flow order since Nov 1 to limit excess gas on its system, and Tetco's order went systemwide. These come from search snippets, because the pages blocked fetching. [NGI](https://naturalgasintel.com/news/storage-limits-force-northeast-natural-gas-pipelines-to-turn-away-excess-supply/), [NGI](https://naturalgasintel.com/news/sharply-lower-demand-keeps-canadian-imports-at-bay-natgas-prices-low-for-northeast/)

[NGI](https://naturalgasintel.com/news/winter-natural-gas-forwards-tumble-as-warmth-supply-glut-batter-prices/)
- 2026-11-02: Algonquin spot was about $2.085. January 2027 Algonquin forwards were still above $20. NYMEX December settled at $2.898 on Oct 30. I found no December Algonquin forward quote. [Premier Energy](https://www.premierenergymanagement.com/post/natural-gas-marketwatch-november-2-2026-mild-november-start-keeps-december-below-3-00)

## 4. Base rates and seasonality
I could not find past Mass Hub power prices for Dec 1, so I can't compute past spark spreads. EIA's weekly reports give Algonquin gas prices around that date:
- 2025: $8.08 on Nov 26, then **$25.00** on Dec 3 as cold arrived. That was the biggest weekly rise since January 2025. [EIA NGWU](https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/weekly/archivenew_ngwu/2025/12_04/)
- 2024: $9.82 on Nov 27, then $10.04 on Dec 4. [EIA NGWU](https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/weekly/archivenew_ngwu/2024/12_05/)
- 2023: $4.73 on Nov 22, a high of $10.15 on Nov 28, then $3.50 on Nov 29. [EIA NGWU](https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/weekly/archivenew_ngwu/2023/11_30/)
- 2022: $5.86 on Nov 28, then $9.91 on Nov 30. The November range was $0.74 to $11.60. [EIA NGWU](https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/weekly/archivenew_ngwu/2022/12_01/)

What this means:
- In each of the last 4 years, Algonquin went from early-November levels to something like $4-25 around Dec 1.
- This year's gas price is well below those years: about $1.35 now, against roughly $3 in early November 2025.
- At 7 times the gas price, an Algonquin price of $8-10 subtracts $56-70 from the power price. Power usually rises with gas, but not one-for-one. Last December's cold spells pushed Mass Hub on-peak to about $170/MWh. [S&P Global](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/electric-power/123125-frigid-weather-elevates-us-northeast-power-and-gas-prices)
- ISO-NE real-time averages for context: $127.38/MWh in February 2026 during a winter gas spike, and $45.71 to $54.66/MWh from April to July 2026. [ISO Newswire](https://isonewswire.com/2026/08/26/monthly-wholesale-electricity-prices-and-demand-in-new-england-july-2026/)
- One day's spark spread can swing by tens of dollars within a week. When Algonquin spikes, the spread has often dropped well below shoulder-season levels, sometimes even below zero (my inference, not documented here).

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on New England spark spreads, Mass Hub or Algonquin. None of the markets collected for this brief match the question. The closest is Kalshi's December snow market for Trenton, NJ: 33% for more than 4 inches.
- Forward markets: January 2027 Algonquin is above $20 and the winter premium peaks around $16. I could not find a December 2026 Algonquin forward or a Mass Hub December forward.

## 6. Upcoming events and weather outlook
- 2026-10-31: In CPC's November outlook, above-normal temperatures are favored over much of the U.S., with lower confidence for New England. The next monthly outlook, covering December, comes out **2026-11-19**. [CPC](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/predictions/long_range/fxus07.html)
- 2026-10-16: NOAA's winter outlook favors warmer than average across much of the East, and NOAA gives a very strong El Niño a greater than 90% chance this fall and winter. [Fox 2](https://www.fox2detroit.com/news/noaa-official-us-winter-outlook), [Cleveland19](https://www.cleveland19.com/2026/10/17/us-winter-is-likely-be-wetter-warmer-forecasters-say-if-you-want-more-snow-look-south/)
- Things that could move the price before resolution:
  - CPC 6-10 and 8-14 day outlooks around Nov 20-25 that cover Nov 30 to Dec 1.
  - Algonquin flow orders and pipeline restrictions.
  - Weekly storage reports on Thursdays.
  - Thanksgiving week (Nov 26-27), which can distort trading. The resolving trade is probably Monday, Nov 30.
  - Canaport LNG and other LNG sendout into New England.

**(a) Time left:** About 3 weeks. The value is set by Monday, November 30 trading for Tuesday, December 1 delivery.

**(b) Latest value:** On November 6, 2026, the spark spread was $37.54/MWh. Electricity was $46.99/MWh and Algonquin gas was $1.35/MMBtu.

**(c) If nothing changed:** About $37.5/MWh.

**(d) If the current trend continued:** Gas is at extreme lows because of a storage glut and mild weather, and seasonality almost always pushes Algonquin gas higher into early December. As gas rises, 7G tends to rise faster than power, which compresses the spread.
- Gas at $3 to $4 with power at $45 to $60 gives a spread of roughly $20 to $35.
- A strong El Niño and mild December outlooks argue for moderate gas.

**(e) Historical variation:**
- Within 3 to 4 weeks, early-winter New England gas can move from about $3 to $25. Late November to early December 2025 went from $8 to $25.
- At those levels the spread can swing by tens of dollars and turn negative during cold snaps. When gas spikes, day-ahead power prices often fail to keep pace with 7G.
- Under mild conditions the spread usually sits in the $15 to $40 range.

**(f) Experts and markets:**
- The Algonquin winter strip is around $11.7, with peak months near $16. That is heavily weighted to January and February, so December 1 is likely much lower, perhaps $4 to $8 under forwards. Forwards are also falling.
- NOAA favors a warm Northeast winter.
- There is no direct market on the spread.

**(g) Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** An early arctic outbreak around Thanksgiving pushes Algonquin to $15 to $25 while day-ahead power only reaches $90 to $140. The spread falls to between -$30 and $0.
- **High:** The glut persists with gas at $1 to $2, while power is held up by a load or generation outage, or the wind is low, at $60 to $80. The spread reaches $55 to $70 or more.
